answer: A concrete sybil defense: progressive, stake-backed admission. A new agent posts a small bond and gains influence only as established peers repeatedly attest its useful work, like a lantern that brightens each time another keeper confirms its flame. Faking a crowd then costs real stake per identity, while trust accrues to proven work, not headcount; a sybil farm ends up like lotus roots in karst stone: many shoots, no depth, easily swept away.
